title: Shipping AI Into 5 Major Banks Without a 12-Month Compliance Wait — Al Chen, Cisco
talk_summary: A Cisco engineer describes how they cut bank AI deployment from a year to weeks by treating compliance as an evidence problem: proving CVEs are actually gone, proving backups are actually correct, and proving judges don't leak PII. The transferable core is 'show your work' — automated harnesses that verify claims rather than check boxes.

takeaways.technique: Exploit-verification harness instead of version-bump checks
takeaways.what_they_do: They build a 'harbor task' — instructions + dockerized app environment + pass/fail tests — and have an agent write an exploit against the old vulnerable version, then test whether the bumped version still permits it, running many parallel trials in sandboxes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I want you to go and write an exploit based on the older version to see if this new version still has that exploit. Then write a test to see if that exploit actually passed or not.

takeaways.what_they_do: They refuse to accept a checkbox result; every claim (CVE fixed, backup valid) must be backed by an independent check — row counts, replica convergence, exploit tests — because the job's success status says nothing about actual correctness.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's about data correctness, and not necessarily just checking a box and seeing if the backup and restore job ran.

takeaways.technique: Judge reasoning suppression + redacted second judge
takeaways.what_they_do: LLM-judge scores always persist, but judge reasoning is only shown if a check confirms no sensitive data; optionally a second judge runs on redacted input so its reasoning is safe to display.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the reasoning for that judge is not persisted. The score, however, you want that score ... that always persists

takeaways.technique: Audit judge system prompts for PII leakage
takeaways.what_they_do: They found an innocuous line in a judge prompt ('so the human reviewer can verify') that let the judge un-redact PII/MNPI in its reasoning, invisible in the UI but present in backend traces.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your LLM as LLM as judges reasoning may un-redact customer information and sensitive information.

takeaways.technique: Parallel sandboxed trials for verification tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: They run the same harness task across many docker/modal/Daytona sandboxes in parallel to get multiple trials and measure agent performance distribution rather than a single run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run these all in parallel, and you have a bunch of trials to see how the agent performed over various trials.

takeaways.technique: Split problems into engineering / workflow / human workstreams
takeaways.what_they_do: When a customer problem arrives, they decompose it into engineering, workflow, and human/organizational streams and automate what they can, explicitly tracking the non-technical remainder.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We break those problems down into uh engineering, workflow, and human and organizational work streams.
